content:
Justin Timberlake has rejected the longstanding rumor that his 2006 hit song “What Goes Around… Comes Around” was written about one of his most famous exes.

Fans long believed that the tune from his album “FutureSex/LoveSounds” was about his ex-girlfriend, Britney Spears. The rumors went on for years despite the fact that the song was released more than four years after the famous couple’s messy split.

Timberlake and Spears dated from 1999 to 2002.

“Maybe I should dispel a rumor at this point, which has gone around forever, which is like, it’s not a personal story from mine,” Timberlake, 45, said on Complex’s “Re-Rank” YouTube series. “It’s actually a personal story from a friend’s. I asked permission.”

The singer said he was inspired to write the song after his friend opened up to him about a rough breakup he was facing. He did not name the friend.

“He was just going through it, and he was telling me what had happened and I said, ‘Do you mind if I write about this?’ And I quote, my friend said, ‘Yeah, torch that bitch. What goes around comes around,’” Timberlake recalled.

Timberlake said his creative juices instantly began flowing so he quickly ended his chat with his friend so he could write the song.

“I was like, ‘I have to go. Thank you,’” he recalled telling his friend. “This song was written in, I mean, damn near 20 minutes. Like, it was just flowing. The interlude that goes with it ... and then you put the video with it, there’s a 10-minute video we shot for it, like this just hit on all cylinders for me.”

Fans jumped to conclusions that the popular track about betrayal and karma was a dig at Spears considering Timberlake suggested in a 2006 GQ interview that his 2002 hit song “Cry Me a River” was inspired by his breakup with Spears.

Fans had long speculated years before that the latter breakup anthem was about the pop star after the song’s music video featured a blonde woman who looked like Spears, further fueling public speculation. Spears said she faced intense media scrutiny over the hearsay at the time.

In Spears’ 2023 memoir “The Woman in Me,” the singer mourned being described by news publications back then “as a harlot who’d broken the heart of America’s golden boy.” She alleged that Timberlake had actually cheated on her multiple times during their relationship.

“The truth: I was comatose in Louisiana, and he was happily running around Hollywood,” she wrote. “May I just say that on his explosive album and in all the press that surrounded it, Justin neglected to mention the several times he’d cheated on me?”

Spears argued that “there’s always more leeway in Hollywood for men than for women,” adding, “And I see how men are encouraged to talk trash about women in order to become famous and powerful. But I was shattered.”

Elsewhere in her memoir, Spears confessed she cheated back on Timberlake with dancer and choreographer Wade Robson after discovering that Timberlake had slept around behind her back while they were together.
